html:
SMTO-CFG-0047 — SMTO can't start because its port number is out of range

GUID: f3e0a0fb-8078-483a-bd6d-3765dd343c84
Slug: config-server-port-must-be-between-1-and
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while starting because its port — the number after the colon in SMTO's web address — is set outside 1 to 65535. Your conversations and settings were not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the config.yaml file in the SMTO folder, or the file named after --config in the command that starts SMTO. Find the port: line under server:. SMTO reads its port number from that line every time it starts.
  2. Change the number to 8011, SMTO's usual port, or another whole number from 1 to 65535. You can also delete the port: line to use 8011. A network port must be in that range, so any other number stops SMTO from starting.
  3. Save the file, then select Start again on the startup screen, or start SMTO the way you normally do. SMTO only reads config.yaml when it starts, so the new port takes effect on the next start.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready and SMTO opens in your browser.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't send config.yaml itself, because it can contain your Model access key, and don't change other lines in it to make this error go away.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Startup configuration validation rejected server.port (config.yaml server.port, checked by ServerConfig.validate_server and Settings.validate_default_node) because it is not between 1 and 65535.

What this means

  • Application server port validation finds a value at or below zero or above 65535. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Application server port validation finds a value at or below zero or above 65535.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect server.port for the controller application, distinct from Gateway bind/outbound ports.

How to fix it

  • Set server.port in the bootstrap config.yaml (in the Server's working directory, or the file named by AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH or --config) to an integer from 1 to 65535, or remove it to use the default 8011, then restart the Server. This is the application server port; it is separate from the launcher's --port/AOR_PORT value and from Gateway bind ports.
  • Set server.port to the intended available service port from 1 through 65535.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended application port in 1–65535 passes startup validation.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
